steps.title: Three new ways to start a sentence
body: A1 sentences always started with the topic — the thing you're talking about. A2 adds two more shapes: the verb can come first (ذَهَبَ الرَّجُلُ — literally "went the man"), and كَانَ can open a sentence to put it in the past.
Two nouns side by side, with no word for "of", also make a whole phrase on their own — بَابُ الْبَيْتِ (the door of the house). No linking word needed.
The tiles below are whole words, matching sentences you've already read. Rebuild each one in the right order.

steps.title: Seven sentences, three shapes
steps.intro: Read each sentence and notice which of the three shapes it uses. You'll rebuild these from word tiles next.

steps.title: Verb or subject first?
steps.explanation: Arabic's verbal sentence is verb-first (VSO) — ذَهَبَ (went) comes before الرَّجُلُ (the man), the reverse of A1's topic-first nominal sentence.

steps.title: You wrote A2's three sentence shapes
steps.message: Verb-first sentences, كَانَ putting a description in the past, and two nouns combining with no linking word — all three built from word tiles, ready for the Review view.
